description: This topic belongs to the branch of physics that studies waves, the propagation of sound, and their properties. It is a crucial, high-yield topic for General Science in competitive examinations.

sections.title: Basics of Wave Motion
sections.description: A wave is a disturbance that transfers energy from one place to another without the net transfer of matter, as particles of the medium vibrate about their mean positions.

key_concepts.explanation: Waves that require a physical medium (solid, liquid, or gas) to propagate. Sound waves and water waves are prime examples.
Waves that do not require a material medium and can travel through a vacuum. Light waves, radio waves, and X-rays are examples.
Waves in which the particles of the medium vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave propagation. Light is a transverse wave.
Waves in which the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation. Sound is a longitudinal wave.

important_facts.fact: Sound waves cannot travel through a vacuum; they strictly require a material medium to propagate.

sections.title: Properties of Sound Waves
sections.description: The characteristics of sound are determined by its physical parameters such as frequency, amplitude, and wavelength.

key_concepts.explanation: The distance between two consecutive crests (or compressions) or two consecutive troughs (or rarefactions).
The total number of vibrations or oscillations occurring in one second. Its SI unit is Hertz (Hz). The pitch of a sound depends directly on its frequency.
The maximum displacement of vibrating particles from their mean position. It determines the loudness or intensity of the sound.
The characteristic of sound that differentiates a shrill sound from a flat or grave sound. A higher frequency produces a higher pitch.

scientific_principles.application: Used to calculate the speed of a wave in any given medium if its frequency and wavelength are known.

sections.title: Speed of Sound and Affecting Factors
sections.description: The speed of sound varies across different mediums and is heavily influenced by factors like temperature, humidity, and density.

important_facts.fact: The speed of sound is maximum in solids, intermediate in liquids, and minimum in gases.
At 0°C, the average speed of sound in dry air is approximately 332 m/s.
For every 1°C increase in temperature, the speed of sound in air increases by 0.61 m/s.
The speed of sound in humid air is greater than in dry air because the density of humid air is lower than that of dry air.
A change in atmospheric pressure has no effect on the speed of sound, provided the temperature remains constant.

sections.title: Acoustic Phenomena
sections.description: When sound waves interact with physical obstacles or different mediums, they exhibit phenomena like reflection, refraction, and resonance.

key_concepts.explanation: The repetition of sound caused by the reflection of sound waves from a distant, hard surface.
The persistence of sound in a closed space or large hall due to multiple overlapping reflections after the source has stopped producing sound.
A phenomenon that occurs when the natural frequency of an object matches the frequency of an applied external force, causing a massive increase in amplitude.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The change in the apparent frequency of a wave as observed by an observer moving relative to the source of the wave.
scientific_principles.application: Utilized in police radar guns, SONAR, and in astronomy to measure the speed at which stars and galaxies are moving away or towards Earth.

important_facts.fact: To hear a distinct echo, the minimum distance between the sound source and the reflecting surface must be approximately 17.2 meters at standard room temperature.

sections.title: Sonic Ranges and Practical Applications
sections.description: Sound waves are categorized based on their frequency ranges, with different ranges having distinct real-world and biological applications.

key_concepts.explanation: Sound waves with frequencies below 20 Hz. Inaudible to humans, but utilized by elephants, whales, and rhinos for communication.
Sound waves with frequencies ranging from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz (20 kHz), which can be detected by the normal human ear.
Sound waves with frequencies above 20,000 Hz (20 kHz). Highly utilized in medical imaging (ultrasound) and industrial flaw detection.

key_associations.extra_info: Employs ultrasonic waves to measure ocean depth and map underwater topographies or locate submarines.
Emit ultrasonic squeaks to navigate in the dark and locate prey by listening to the returning echoes.
Ratio of an object's speed to the speed of sound. A Mach number > 1 indicates supersonic speed (e.g., fighter jets).
